newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai ministry sees 1997/98 coffee output falling.
newsitem.headline: Thai ministry sees 1997/98 coffee output falling.

text.p: Thailand's coffee output for the 1997/98 crop year (October-November) was forecast at 75,741 tonnes, down from 79,027 tonnes during previous crop year, an agriculture ministry official said on Monday.
The agricultural minitry also forecast that the 1997/98 planting area would drop to 66,822.5 hectares from 68,711 hectares during 1996/97.
The yield is projected to drop slightly to 1.13 tonnes per hectare from 1.14 in the previous year.
But a commerce ministry official told Reuters the agriculture ministry's reduced forecast was "modest" and expected the actual output to be higher.
"For the year 1996/97, we based our trade figure on the output projection of 83,000 tonnes, which was derived from both official and trade sources," said a senior commerce ministry official.

"If the weather is agreeable, the output should be better than the forecast figure as planters are likely to grow more. The world prices are not too bad and local consumption has increased quite impressively," he added.
The export target for the 1996/97 crop year was 53,000 tonnes. The target for 1997/98 crop year will be set in October, said the commerce ministry official.
Thailand exports only Robusta FAQ (Fair Average Quality) grade which is normally traded at a discount to LIFFE.
